A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same joint prompt attribution work, renamed from XPrompt to JoPA. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable matching of retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.3 report original faithfulness, runtime, convergence and ablation results using LLaMA-2 (7B-Chat) and Vicuna (7B).

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds original larger-sample, repeated-seed, larger-model, reasoning, jailbreak-detection and attribution-comparison results.

M1.justification: Equation (3) and Algorithm 1 retain the binary-mask objective, gradient-guided initialization and sampling, token swaps, and acceptance procedure. Renaming XPrompt to JoPA and applying it to additional scenarios do not establish a changed proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The original Alpaca, tldr_news and MHC coverage remains. V2 adds AQuA few-shot chain-of-thought reasoning in Appendix A.12 and adversarial jailbreak scenarios involving GCG and random-search prompts in A.4, substantially broadening the evaluated task and input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds averaged Attention and Last-Attention alongside the retained Random, Captum and Integrated-Gradient baselines. Table 8 adds continuous-mask Gradient optimization, and Figure 9 evaluates ReAGent adapted to explain full outputs. These materially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the stated PR definition from a raw joint-probability ratio to a length-normalized ratio; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. New settings include expanded Alpaca/tldr_news sampling and full MHC evaluation, a 20-instance 16-bit LLaMA-2 70B test, and few-shot reasoning. The convergence experiment extends from 100 to 150 iterations.

E4.justification: The original token-count and gradient-guidance ablations remain in Appendices A.6-A.7. V2 adds continuous-mask optimization analysis, jailbreak detection and token-removal cases, diagnosis of ignored requests, and additional counterfactual response examples in A.4, A.5 and A.10. It also extends the convergence analysis.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without stated repeated-seed uncertainty. V2 Appendix A.9 and Table 7 report three runs with different seeds and mean plus standard deviation for all evaluated metrics across the three LLaMA-2 7B datasets. This introduces substantive uncertainty reporting without establishing v1's run count.

E6.justification: Most matched Table 1 entries and all Table 2 timings remain unchanged. For the proposed method on LLaMA-2, Alpaca BLEU changes from 0.482 to 0.484, while MHC PR/KL change from 0.710/0.238 to 0.701/0.246. V2 adds extensive results in Tables 4 and 6-8 and Figures 7-9. The PR change cannot be treated as a same-definition performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a one-swap local-optimum definition and a brief convergence proof sketch, absent from v1. Section 5.2 also revises the mathematical definition of PR through length normalization. The original optimization objective and generation equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about joint attribution, efficient probabilistic search, faithfulness and transferability remain. V2's introduction adds an explicit contribution claim concerning potential benefits to model safety and efficiency, modestly extending the claimed applications.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning jailbreak defense, diagnosis of overlooked requests and stability across seeds. The original token-interaction rationale and black-box mechanism limitation remain. Section 5.3 also introduces an erroneous reference to higher SentenceBert scores indicating greater semantic change, contradicting its lower-is-better definition and Table 1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and documents details such as 16-bit execution for the 70B experiment and ReAGent's full-output adaptation. Existing software and hardware disclosures remain. The new larger-sample runtime limit is inconsistently documented as 240 hours in A.8 and 200 hours in Table 6.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds substantive distinctions from Archipelago and Diffmask. Additional references support attention explanations, ContextCite, jailbreak testing and reasoning experiments. The central positioning around joint attribution of complete generations and most existing related work remain.

P1.justification: V2 renames the method and title, adds equal-contribution credit, corrects and condenses prose, and introduces related-work subsections. It moves the main ablation discussion to Appendix A.6 and the existing limitations paragraph to Section 7. Much of the original exposition remains.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 1 with attention-baseline rows, adds four result tables and three comparison charts, and redraws the convergence plot with a longer iteration axis. Existing case-study figures and ablation plots are relocated and renumbered, while the timing and dataset tables are reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's small-sample empirical foundation through larger evaluations, additional attribution comparators and three-seed uncertainty reporting. The 70B and reasoning tests further support applicability. Missing Captum results in the larger-sample evaluation, briefly documented new protocols, the informal convergence argument, and reporting inconsistencies limit some additions, but the evidence supporting the central method is substantially broader and better assessed.
